transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because for the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. No matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I draw blood for a living, so I know what I'm looking at. I know they're being altered, and honestly, trying to get anyone to listen to me is just really wearing me down.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

No, I don't hear voices. I haven't experienced anything like that. I mean, I'm not imagining things in my head. This is just about the physical lab results that I'm looking at. So, no, I don't hear anyone talking to me when I'm alone.
Have you had a period when you felt unusually energized or high, like you needed much less sleep than usual?

No, not at all. I haven't felt anything like that. If anything, I'm just exhausted from trying to get to the bottom of all this. I definitely still need my sleep every night, so... no, I haven't had any periods where I felt super energized or high.
Aside from the lab results, do you believe anyone is trying to harm, monitor, or interfere with you personally?

No, nothing like that. Um, I don't think anyone is out to get me or following me around or anything. I'm not worried about my own safety. It's really just... it's strictly about my dad's chart and what they're doing with his numbers. I'm just trying to get that fixed. So, no, nobody is trying to harm or monitor me personally.
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts seem hard to follow or jump from topic to topic?

No, nobody has ever told me that. I mean, I communicate pretty clearly. I work as a phlebotomist, so I kind of have to be clear and precise when I'm talking to people at work. My thoughts don't really jump around at all... I'm just very focused on the facts and the numbers in my dad's chart. So, no, I haven't had anyone say I'm hard to follow.
Other than the issue with your dad’s lab results, have you had any experiences of seeing things that other people could not see?

No, I haven't. I don't see things that aren't there. Um, my vision is perfectly normal. Everything I'm looking at is right there in black and white on my dad's chart, so... no, I've never experienced anything like that.
Has this issue with your dad’s lab results caused problems for you at work or in your day-to-day life?

Yeah, it actually has. Um, with my family, they've started leaving me out of some of the planning for his appointments. I think they just don't want to deal with me bringing up the chart errors. And at work... well, it's definitely affecting things there, too. I mean, I feel like I'm no longer being considered for lab supervision. People seem to think I make record issues too confrontational now, just because I insist on the numbers being accurate. So, yes, it is causing some problems.
Has a doctor told you that you have any neurological or other medical condition affecting your brain?

No, I don't have any brain conditions or anything like that. I've never been diagnosed with any neurological problems. My brain is fine, I just... I just want people to look at the actual lab results.
Over the past year, have you found yourself losing interest or motivation in things you used to care about?

No, not really. I mean, I still care about my work and my family. I haven't lost interest in anything. I'm just focused on getting this situation with my dad's chart sorted out, you know? That's what's taking up most of my attention right now, but I haven't lost motivation for the things I normally care about.
Do you believe it is actually possible for people in the clinic system to secretly change your dad’s lab results after they are entered?

Yes, I do. I mean, I'm a phlebotomist, so I know how these systems operate. That's basically what all this is about. For the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or... or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s wearing me down, honestly, having to fight everyone on this. But yes, I know it's possible because it's happening.
Have you had trouble taking care of yourself, like keeping up with hygiene or basic daily tasks?

No, I don't have any trouble with that. I mean, outside of the whole dispute about my dad's records, I'm functioning normally. I still go to all my phlebotomy shifts, I pay my bills on time, I take care of myself... I manage all my normal day-to-day responsibilities just fine. It's really just this one thing that's taking up so much of my energy, but it hasn't stopped me from doing what I need to do to live my life.
Do you believe your dad’s lab results are being changed in a way that could really happen in the clinic’s computer system, or in a way that would be impossible in real life?

It's definitely something that can really happen. I mean, it's not magic or anything impossible. Like I said, I work with these systems, so I know how they're set up. It's really just someone going into the computer and changing the numbers. It is a completely real thing that someone can do if they have the right access in the system.
Is there any chance you could be mistaken about your dad’s lab results being changed?

No, there is zero chance I'm mistaken. I know I've already brought this up, but I have spent the entire last year trying to prove that someone is holding back or altering those results. My family and the doctors keep telling me the numbers are fine, but they aren't. I know what I saw, and the chart simply does not match. I am not wrong about this, even though it's completely wearing me down that no one will just believe me.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being inserted, removed, or controlled by someone else?

No, definitely not. I mean, my thoughts are my own. Nobody is putting things in my head or taking them out, or controlling what I think. I just know what I know about my dad's records, but that's from my own eyes and my own experience, not from anyone controlling me.
Have you ever felt that someone was controlling your actions or movements?
No, I haven't ever felt anything like that. I control my own body and my own actions. Nobody is forcing me to move or... or doing things through me. I'm in complete control of myself.
Have people close to you noticed that you’ve become emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to be?

No, my family hasn't mentioned anything like that. I mean, I'm still just me. I get upset, I get happy, and I show it. If anything, they probably think I'm a little too expressive right now because I get so worked up and frustrated about my dad's situation. But no, I haven't become emotionally flat or blank, and nobody has told me I have.
Other than your dad’s lab results, have you had any other fixed beliefs that other people say are not true?

No, not really. I mean, it's just this one thing with my dad's records. I don't have any other... beliefs like that. Everything else in my life is pretty normal. I go to work, I do my job... it's just this one situation that people are telling me isn't real, even though I know what I saw. But no, nothing else.
Did your certainty that your dad’s lab results were being changed come on suddenly over a short period of time?

No, it wasn't sudden at all. It was more like... well, working in the lab, you just start to notice little inconsistencies over time. At first, it was just a number here or there that didn't make sense with his previous blood work. I brushed it off a few times, thinking maybe it was just a calibration error or something. But then it kept happening, and I started keeping track. It was a gradual realization that someone was deliberately altering his files. It took months of putting the pieces together before I was absolutely certain.
During this past year, have you had a period of feeling deeply depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I haven't been depressed. I mean, it's been a stressful year, obviously, dealing with all this stuff with my dad's lab work, but I'm not depressed. I don't feel sad or down all day. I'm just trying to figure out what's going on and get people to listen to me. But no, I haven't had any periods of feeling deeply depressed.
Aside from this issue with your dad’s lab results, have you had times when your behavior became noticeably disorganized or odd to other people?

No, not at all. I mean, like I said, everything else is completely normal. I go to work, I draw blood, I interact with patients and my coworkers just fine. Nobody has ever said I was acting strange or... or disorganized. I just do my job. It's really only this one issue with the lab records. Aside from that, I'm just a regular person.
